The Python internship in short

The SkillMe Python internship is a 4-week, fully remote programme open to students worldwide. Over four weekly milestones you build one of 3 projects, such as PyAnalytics: Local Automation & Data Processing Hub, post each milestone publicly on LinkedIn, and have it reviewed against clear acceptance criteria. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month, and interns who get 3 of 4 milestones approved earn a QR-verified certificate and a Letter of Recommendation.

What you build

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

You are assigned one of these projects when you start, and build it milestone by milestone.

PyAnalytics: Local Automation & Data Processing Hub

Build a friendly Python tool that reads your spending data from CSV files, cleans it up and turns it into clear reports, ending with a small web dashboard.

  1. W1Read a CSV and Summarise It
  2. W2Classes, Modules and Clean Data
  3. W3Save to SQLite and Handle Errors
  4. W4Web Dashboard, Tests and Demo

PySentinel: Automated Web Intelligence & System Monitor

Build a Python monitor that checks your computer's health and whether your favourite websites are up, and tells you when something goes wrong.

  1. W1System Health Snapshot
  2. W2Configurable Checks with Classes
  3. W3Website Uptime Checks with requests
  4. W4Scheduled Monitoring, Alerts and Tests

QuizCraft: Flashcard & Quiz Trainer

Build a quiz and flashcard app that helps you revise any subject, starting in the terminal and ending as a small web app.

  1. W1Terminal Quiz from a Text File
  2. W2Decks, Classes and Saved Progress
  3. W3Import Questions from a Free API
  4. W4Web Quiz with Flask and Tests
Week by week

What each week of the Python internship covers

Shown for PyAnalytics: Local Automation & Data Processing Hub. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Read a CSV and Summarise It

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Write a small Python program that reads a CSV file of expenses and prints useful totals in the terminal. This is the foundation of the whole project, and it practises the everyday Python skills (functions, loops, files and dictionaries) that every later week depends on.

    What you learn

    • Reading files safely with with open(...) and the built-in csv module
    • Splitting a program into small functions that each do one job
    • Using dictionaries to group and total values by category
    • Building a simple text menu with input() and a while loop

    What you submit

    • main.py with separate functions for loading, totalling and displaying data
    • A sample data/expenses.csv file with at least 15 rows
    • A working menu-driven CLI you can run with python main.py
    • A README with run instructions and a screenshot of the output
  2. Week 2 of 4

    Classes, Modules and Clean Data

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Reorganise your code into classes and modules, and make it handle messy real-world data. You will also let users add new expenses and export a report, so the tool starts to feel like a real app.

    What you learn

    • Writing classes with __init__ and methods (an Expense and an ExpenseTracker)
    • Splitting code into modules and importing between files
    • Cleaning and validating data such as blank rows, bad numbers and extra spaces
    • Writing data back to files as CSV and JSON

    What you submit

    • tracker.py, storage.py and main.py modules with classes in use
    • A loader that reports how many bad rows it skipped
    • New menu options for adding, searching and exporting
    • A generated report.json committed as a sample output
  3. Week 3 of 4

    Save to SQLite and Handle Errors

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Replace the CSV file with a real SQLite database using Python's built-in sqlite3 module, and add proper command-line arguments. This teaches you how most apps store data and how to make a program fail gracefully.

    What you learn

    • Creating tables and running INSERT and SELECT queries with sqlite3
    • Using parameterised queries (? placeholders) to avoid SQL injection
    • Handling errors with try/except and giving clear messages
    • Adding command-line arguments and subcommands with argparse

    What you submit

    • db.py with table creation and query functions
    • CLI subcommands import, add and summary (with --month)
    • Friendly error messages for missing files and bad input
    • An updated README listing every command with an example
  4. Week 4 of 4

    Web Dashboard, Tests and Demo

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Put a small web dashboard on top of your database using Flask, and protect your core logic with a few automated tests. You finish with a complete, documented project that you can demo in under a minute.

    What you learn

    • Creating routes and HTML templates with Flask
    • Handling a simple HTML form with GET and POST
    • Writing unit tests with pytest
    • Writing a clear README for someone who has never seen your project

    What you submit

    • A Flask dashboard with summary, expense list and add-expense pages
    • At least 4 passing pytest tests
    • requirements.txt and a complete README with screenshots
    • A 30-60 second demo video
What you get

What the Python internship gives you

Stipend for top performers

Up to $100 a month for the interns whose reviewed work stands out in their cohort. It is earned, not handed out.

Review by working engineers

Engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn review submissions, so submit mindfully. Work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

How to apply

  1. Take the 5-minute quiz. Eight questions on the basics of Python 3, OOP, APIs.
  2. Tell us why you want in. A person reads every application. Anyone can apply, but selection is competitive.
  3. Get shortlisted. If you are selected you hear back within 48 hours and receive your offer letter.
  4. Build and submit weekly. One milestone a week for four weeks, each one reviewed.
Apply for the Python internship

Python internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the Python internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: PyAnalytics: Local Automation & Data Processing Hub, PySentinel: Automated Web Intelligence & System Monitor or QuizCraft: Flashcard & Quiz Trainer. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

Is the Python internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. The stipend is performance-based and is not paid to every intern: it goes to the interns whose reviewed work stands out in their cohort.

Who reviews my work?

Every weekly submission is reviewed against that week's acceptance criteria by the SkillMe team, which includes engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Work that misses the bar comes back with notes on what to fix.

Do I need experience to apply for the Python internship?

You need the basics of Python 3, OOP, APIs, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at Beginner level and week 4 reaches Intermediate+. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How long is the internship and how much time does it take?

It runs for 4 weeks with one milestone a week. Each milestone is planned for about 2-3 hours, and it is fully remote, so you work at your own pace around college or a job.

Who can apply? Is it open outside India?

Anyone can apply, from any country, college or year, and we encourage you to. Selection is competitive: every application is read by a person, and shortlisted applicants hear back within 48 hours.

What do I get when I finish?

An offer letter when you are selected, a public portfolio page with every approved milestone, and a QR-verified certificate and Letter of Recommendation once 3 of your 4 milestones are approved. Top performers also earn the stipend and are referred to hiring partners.
